info.title: Ariadne Daemon API
info.description: REST API of ariadned, the coding-agent orchestrator daemon.

get.summary: List agent events (poll with `after` for tailing).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return items with id greater than this.

get.summary: Subscribe to the live domain-event stream.
get.description:
Every state change in the daemon — from HTTP calls, from the scheduler and
from agent activity alike — is published here. Each message carries a fresh
ULID `id`, the event kind as its `event` name, and the full updated DTO as
`data`, so clients patch their state without refetching.

There is **no replay or backfill**: the `id` is informational and
`Last-Event-ID` is ignored. On (re)connect, refetch the REST state you care
about and then follow the stream.

A client that falls too far behind loses events. It is never left silently
stale: the daemon sends a final `resync` event (`{"missed": n}`) and closes
the connection, so an `EventSource` reconnects and takes the refetch path
above.

parameters.name: goal
parameters.description: Only events belonging to this goal.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Only events belonging to this task.

200.description: SSE stream of domain events (text/event-stream). No replay on reconnect: refetch REST state first. A lagging client gets a final `resync` event (ResyncDto) and the connection is closed.

get.summary: Recent daemon log lines from the in-memory ring buffer, oldest first.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: Return only the last N lines.

get.description:
The stream opens with a `snapshot` event carrying the current ring buffer
(a `LogSnapshotResponse`, what `GET /v1/logs` would have returned), then
sends a `delta` event per new line (a `LogLineDto`). Payloads are compact
JSON, so log content cannot break SSE framing. There is no replay on
reconnect: every connection starts over from a fresh snapshot, which is
also the resync path for a follower that fell behind and was dropped.

200.description: SSE stream of daemon log lines (text/event-stream). A `snapshot` event with the current buffer (LogSnapshotResponse), then a `delta` event per new line (LogLineDto). A follower that falls too far behind is disconnected; reconnecting starts over from a fresh snapshot.

post.summary: Type into a session's pane: the write counterpart of the log stream.
post.description:
The bytes go to tmux verbatim, so the agent sees exactly what was typed in
front of it and the echo comes back through `/logs/stream` like any other
pane output. Nothing is appended — a submit carries its own `\r`.

Both halves of "live" are checked, as in `logs_stream`: the row's status,
because a finished session must not be typed into, and tmux itself,
because tmux names are reused and a `send-keys` at a stale name would land
in a successor's pane.

get.summary: Recent tmux pane output of a session.

get.description:
The stream opens with a `resize` event (`SessionPaneSize`) carrying the
grid the output is drawn at: the snapshot is wrapped at that width and
every later repaint is addressed in it. A live pane is measured; a
finished one is reported at the last size it was seen at, if it ever was.

Then a `snapshot` event carrying the scrollback the `/logs` endpoint would
return — as the pane's screen rather than as text: it ends where the pane's
cursor is (see [`as_screen`]), so the repaints that follow land where they
were addressed. Then a `delta` event per burst of new output. Both payloads
are a `SessionLogChunk`: raw terminal bytes, escape sequences and all, are
JSON-encoded so they cannot break SSE's line framing.

A pane resized under the stream — by `ariadne attach`, say — sends a
`resize` and a *fresh* `snapshot` rather than continuing with deltas: the
output in flight straddles the change and belongs to neither grid, so the
client starts over at the new one. `snapshot` therefore means "replace
everything you have", whenever it arrives. Nothing is sent in between: a
delta drawn at a grid the client does not have is the corruption this is
all here to avoid. If no coherent screen can be had — the pane cannot be
read, or keeps changing shape while it is — the connection is closed
*without* an `end`, at the opening as much as later on: the session is not
over, and a fresh connection is the shortest way back to a grid and a
screen that agree. Only a pane confirmed gone ends a stream.

When the session ends — or if it was already over when the request arrived
— the remaining output is flushed, a final `end` event (`SessionLogEnd`)
is sent and the connection closes. There is no replay and no
`Last-Event-ID`: reconnecting starts again from a fresh snapshot.

200.description: SSE stream of terminal output (text/event-stream). A `resize` event with the grid the output is drawn at (`{"cols": 80, "rows": 24}`, SessionPaneSize), then a `snapshot` event with the current scrollback and a `delta` event per burst of new output — both `{"chunk": "..."}` (SessionLogChunk). A pane resized under the stream sends a new `resize` followed by a fresh `snapshot`, which replaces everything sent so far. A final `end` event (SessionLogEnd) closes the stream when the session is over.

post.summary:
Revive an ended session: new tmux, same agent conversation (resumed via
the stored internal session id). Returns the session to attach to, which
is this one either way — relaunched under its own id and tmux name, or
untouched when its tmux turned out to be alive already.

get.summary:
Diff of the task branch against its base (`git diff base...branch`), or,
once the task is merged, the diff its merge commit brought into the base —
after the merge the branch is contained in the base, so the three-dot diff
would be forever empty.

AgentKind.description: Which coding-agent CLI a profile runs on.

max_tasks.description: Max tasks the planner may create (default: unbounded).

planner_profile.description: Planner profile id or unique name.

required_approvals.description: Approvals required to merge a task (default 1).

oneOf.description: Omit for auto: the first installed agent CLI is used at spawn time.

prompts.description:
Briefing prompts to seed instead of the role defaults. A kind listed
here replaces its default; every other kind of the role is seeded as
usual. Absent or empty = the role defaults, unedited.

reviewer_profile.description:
Reviewer profile id or name. Derived from the session context when the
call comes from an agent; required for user-submitted reviews.

depends_on.description: Task ids this task depends on.

engineer_profile.description: Engineer profile id or unique name.

repo_id.description: Repo id within the goal; may be omitted when the goal has exactly one repo.

reviewer_profiles.description: Reviewer profile ids or names, in review order. At least one.

DeletedDto.description: Payload of the deletion events: the id of the gone entity.

oneOf.description: Covers status changes: finalize, cancel, completion.

data.description: Covers status changes: finalize, cancel, completion.

oneOf.description: Covers status transitions, edits, stall flags and worktree changes.

data.description: Covers status transitions, edits, stall flags and worktree changes.

oneOf.description: Covers status changes: kill, resume, exit, activity.

data.description: Covers status changes: kill, resume, exit, activity.

oneOf.description: A raw agent event reported by a hook.

data.description: A raw agent event reported by a hook.

FinalizePlanRequest.description: Body of `POST /v1/goals/{id}/finalize`: planning ends, execution starts.

summary.description: Plan summary, recorded in the goal thread.

status.description: Always "ok" when the daemon is able to answer.

level.description: Log level as tracing prints it.

message.description: Message followed by the event's fields as ` key=value` pairs.

target.description: Module path the event was emitted from.

ts.description: When the event was recorded, RFC 3339.

LogSnapshotResponse.description: Response of `GET /v1/logs`: the in-memory ring buffer, oldest first.

ModelDto.description: One model an agent CLI can run, as served by `GET /v1/models`.

agent_kind.description: The agent CLI this model belongs to.

description.description: One-line capability summary (absent for discovered opencode models).

NewProfilePrompt.description:
One prompt override in [`CreateProfileRequest`]: the kind spelled as on the
prompt routes, and the text to seed instead of the role default.

oneOf.description:
None = auto: resolved at spawn time to the first installed agent CLI
(claude_code, then codex, then opencode).

extra_flags.description: Extra argv flags appended when spawning the agent CLI.

ProfilePromptDto.description: One of the briefing prompts a profile owns beside its system prompt.

content.description: Template text with `{placeholder}` tokens the daemon fills in.

PromptDefaultDto.description:
One built-in prompt default. Unlike [`ProfilePromptDto`] it belongs to no
profile, so there is nothing to timestamp.

content.description: Template text with `{placeholder}` tokens the daemon fills in.

PromptKind.description:
A prompt a profile owns beside its system prompt: the briefing an agent of
that role is started or resumed with. Each kind belongs to exactly one role
(see [`PromptKind::role`]).

base_branch.description: Base branch tasks merge into; defaults to the repo's current branch.

path.description: Absolute path to an existing git repository.

ResyncDto.description:
Payload of the `resync` control event.

Sent as the last message of a connection that fell too far behind: the
daemon dropped `missed` events for it and closes the stream. The client
must refetch its REST state before following the stream again (an
`EventSource` reconnects on its own).

missed.description: Events this connection lost. Informational: they cannot be recovered.

ReviewVerdict.description: Review verdict for one reviewer in one round.

Role.description: The role an agent plays in the orchestration.

RolePromptDefaultsDto.description:
Response of `GET /v1/roles/{role}/prompt-defaults`: what a profile of that
role is seeded with, read without creating or touching anything.

prompts.description: The role's briefing prompts, in briefing order.

internal_session_id.description: Agent-internal id: claude session uuid / codex thread id / opencode session id.

data.description:
Keystrokes to type into the pane, exactly as the terminal produced
them: `\r` for Return, `\x03` for Ctrl-C, `\x1b[A` for Up. Sent
verbatim — nothing is appended, so a submit has to carry its own `\r`.

SessionLogChunk.description:
Payload of the `snapshot` and `delta` events of
`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/logs/stream`.

Terminal output is raw bytes — newlines, escape sequences, control
characters — none of which survive SSE's line-oriented `data:` framing on
their own, so every chunk travels as JSON.

chunk.description: Terminal output as written, decoded lossily from UTF-8.

SessionLogEnd.description:
Payload of the final `end` event of `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/logs/stream`:
the session is over and no further output is coming.

logs.description: Recent pane contents captured from tmux.

SessionPaneSize.description:
Payload of the `resize` event of `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/logs/stream`: the
grid the pane is drawing against, in cells.

A terminal stream only means anything at a size. The agent addresses the
cursor and erases lines against *this* grid, so a viewer that renders the
bytes at any other one has every repaint land on the wrong row.

depends_on.description: Ids of tasks that must merge before this one starts.

reviewer_profile_ids.description: Reviewer profile ids in planner-assigned order.

stalled.description: Set when the agent went idle without advancing the task.

TaskUpdatedDto.description:
Payload of `task_updated`: the task as it now stands, plus the audit row
when the update was a status transition.

oneOf.description: Present when this update was a status transition.

UpdateProfilePromptRequest.description: Body of `PUT /v1/profiles/{id}/prompts/{kind}`: the whole new text.

UpdateProfileRequest.description: Partial update; absent fields stay unchanged.

agent_kind.description:
New agent kind, or "auto" to clear it (resolve the first installed
CLI at spawn time). Absent = unchanged.

model.description:
New model, or "default" (or empty) to clear it back to the agent's
default. Absent = unchanged.

UpdateTaskRequest.description: Partial update; only allowed while the task is pending/ready.
